artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a prime $p$ and a nonzero integer $n$, let $\nu_p(n)$ denote the $p$-adic valuation of $n$ (the largest integer $e\ge 0$ with $p^e\mid n$), with $\nu_p(0)=+\infty$. Prove or disprove the following three claims.

Let $m\in\mathbb{Z}$ satisfy $m\equiv 1\pmod 3$.

(i) For every positive integer $n$,
$$\nu_3\!\left(\frac{1}{n}\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}\binom{n-1}{k}(-1)^k\binom{2k}{k}m^k\right)\;\ge\;\min\{\nu_3(n),\;\nu_3(m-1)\}-1.$$

(ii) For every integer $a>\nu_3(m-1)$,
$$\frac{1}{3^a}\sum_{k=0}^{3^a-1}\binom{3^a-1}{k}(-1)^k\binom{2k}{k}m^k\;\equiv\;-\frac{m-1}{3}\pmod{3^{\nu_3(m-1)}}.$$

(iii) For every integer $a\ge 2$,
$$\sum_{k=0}^{3^a-1}\binom{3^a-1}{k}(-1)^k\binom{2k}{k}\;\equiv\;-3^{2a-1}\pmod{3^{2a}}.$$
artifact.status_search_result: Sun's collection of conjectures on congruences contains many problems involving $\binom{2k}{k}$, and several have been resolved (e.g., Guo–Zeng proved the divisibility conjecture; the congruence $\sum_{k=0}^{q-1}\binom{2k}{k}\equiv q^2\pmod{3q^2}$ for $q$ a power of 3 by Pan–Sun). However, no specific source was found that confirms a proof or disproof of all three parts of this particular conjecture (with the parameter $m\equiv 1\pmod 3$ and the $3$-adic valuation lower bound). Status appears unverified.

status_evidence.title: Proof of Sun's conjecture on the divisibility of certain binomial sums
status_evidence.snippet: Guo–Zeng prove a divisibility conjecture of Z.-W. Sun involving central binomial-type sums.
status_evidence.claim: Some of Sun's binomial-sum conjectures have been proved, but this paper concerns a different divisibility statement.

status_evidence.title: The sum sum_{k=0}^{q-1} C(2k,k) for q a power of 3
status_evidence.snippet: Proves Sun–Tauraso style congruence for sums of central binomial coefficients modulo powers of 3.
status_evidence.claim: A related congruence (the m=1 case shape) has been treated, but the present m-parameter conjecture is not directly addressed.
